Do: Use the past simple with a finished time: yesterday, ago, last year, in 2019. | Use the present perfect when the time is unfinished or not given: ever, never, yet, so far, today.
Don't: Don't say I have seen him yesterday. | Don't use the present simple with since or for to mean up to now: We are married since 2015 is wrong.

Do: Learn each phrasal verb with a full example sentence. | Put a pronoun between the verb and the particle: pick you up, turn it off.
Don't: Don't split three-part verbs: run out of milk, not run out milk. | Don't use to-infinitive after give up: give up smoking, not give up to smoke.

Do: Use contractions: I'm, can't, I've. | Give your reason for writing early, in the first or second line.
Don't: Don't use formal phrases with friends: Yours faithfully, I would be grateful if. | Don't translate Arabic greetings: Respected Sam or I wish you are fine.

Do: Choose the conditional by asking: real or unreal? Present, future or past? | Use were for all persons in formal unreal conditionals: If I were you.
Don't: Never put will or would in the if clause: If I would know is wrong. | Don't use unless + not: unless already means if not.

Do: Learn the verb with its noun as one unit: meet a deadline, do research. | Use make for results you create and do for tasks.
Don't: Don't say make research, catch a deadline, or take attention. | Don't count uncountable nouns: a progress, researches, informations.

Do: State your opinion in the introduction and keep it to the end. | Start each body paragraph with a topic sentence.
Don't: Don't write Although … but … together. | Don't use According to my opinion. Use In my view or I strongly believe.

Do: Invert the auxiliary and subject after Never, Rarely, Little, Not only, No sooner and Under no circumstances. | Add do / does / did when there is no auxiliary, and use the base verb after it.
Don't: With Only when / Only after, don't invert the first clause. Invert the main clause. | Don't invert after Only + a subject: Only Sara knew.

Do: Learn each word's grammar: facilitate + process, advocate + -ing or a noun. | Check uncountable academic nouns: evidence, research, information.
Don't: Don't say facilitate someone to do something. | Don't confuse mitigate (reduce harm) with militate against (work against).

Do: Use headings and the passive to stay impersonal: It was found that… | Make recommendations specific and based on your findings.
Don't: Don't use contractions or I think in a report. | Don't repeat the subject: The aim of this report it is to… is wrong.

Do: Use What … is / was to put the focus at the end. | Use It was … that / who to contrast with something else.
Don't: Don't add an extra it: What I need it is is wrong. | Don't use what in an it-cleft: It is the noise what annoys me is wrong.

Do: Keep idioms exactly as they are. Their words are fixed. | Check the register. Many idioms are journalistic or conversational.
Don't: Don't translate Arabic idioms word for word into English. | Don't confuse sound-alikes: toe / tow the line, moot / mute point.

Do: Cut every word that adds nothing: because, not due to the fact that. | Keep a key term the same throughout.
Don't: Don't change a key word just to avoid repetition (elegant variation). | Don't mix casual and formal registers in one text.
